title: Development happens in the PL chat and in a workspace PL owns
prompt: Where does application development actually happen?
summary: Thinking, discovery and design happen in your PL chat; generation and verification happen in a workspace directory PL owns on the platform host; committed sources land in the platformapps repository with a provenance gate.

layers.title: Workspace and repositories
items: platformapps repository: committed sources, releases, provenance

layers.title: Databases
items: platformapps: one schema per generated app

blocks.caption: You never edit files; PL generates into its workspace and commits with a provenance manifest.

rows.label: Conversation and decisions
rows.value: In your PL project. Every message and approval is an event in the delivery case.

rows.label: Generated code
rows.value: In a per-run workspace directory owned by PL, then committed to the platformapps repository as an immutable release snapshot.

rows.label: Builds and tests
rows.value: In that workspace, with an allow-listed child environment: no platform secrets reach the app processes.

rows.label: Application data
rows.value: A dedicated PostgreSQL schema per application in the platformapps database, with the app's own login.

blocks.text: Today the platform host is a single workstation. That is where the PL API, EAL, UME and the generated apps run. Multi-host deployment is part of the deployment foundation planned for the customer pilot.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL where development happens
plPrompts.prompt: Where does application development actually happen on this platform: which directories, repositories and databases are involved for a generated application? Do not build anything.

title: Deployed to a Local Development landscape and registered with EAL
prompt: Where are applications built by this platform deployed?
summary: Into the landscape you confirmed: today Local defaults, meaning the UI and API run as processes on the platform host with reserved ports and the app's schema in the platformapps database; the release is registered with the EAL registry and roles are published to UME.

blocks.caption: Deployment is part of the same delivery run, not a separate pipeline.

rows: UI and API processes on the platform host, ports reserved by the deployer, schema in platformapps
Independent deployables, release manifests, non-loopback origins
Production-shaped environments promoted by release manifests
Customer-controlled installation with identity, secrets, backup and recovery gates

blocks.text: Where the app is deployed is decided at the landscape step. The nudge Use Local defaults and confirm composes, resolves and confirms the placement in one click. EKG can provide placements when it is online; otherwise Local defaults apply.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL where apps are deployed
plPrompts.prompt: Where are applications built by this platform deployed in this workspace, and what is registered with EAL and UME during deployment? Do not build anything.

title: Applications run as their own processes and are used through EAL
prompt: Where do the deployed applications run?
summary: Each application runs as its own API and UI processes on the platform host, reading and writing its own PostgreSQL schema. Users reach it through EAL, which launches the UI with a signed authority and enforces roles from UME.

blocks.caption: The application never sees the platform's credentials; it holds only its own database login.

rows.label: Processes
rows.value: Two per application (API, UI), started by the PL deployer on reserved ports and adopted on restart through a managed runtime.

rows.label: Data
rows.value: One schema per application in the platformapps database with a dedicated login; row-level security policies in integration-backed apps.

rows.label: Access
rows.value: EAL chat and full view; EAL signs an application authority reference that the API resolves live before it answers.

rows.label: Identity
rows.value: Roles published to UME at release; a test identity pl.app-name.user is created for you to try the app.

blocks.text: Deployed application processes are children of the PL API process today. Restarting the PL API stops them; the managed runtime re-adopts or restarts them. A supervisor for production is part of the planned runtime work.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL where apps run
plPrompts.prompt: Where do the deployed applications run, how do users reach them, and how does an application check who is calling it? Do not build anything.

title: Local Development today; Central Development, QA, UAT and Production are on the roadmap
prompt: What development, testing, staging, and production environments does the platform support?
summary: Local Development is fully supported. The environment ladder to Production is designed (release manifests, environment promotion gates, customer deployment profiles) and sequenced in the roadmap, but not yet available.

items.label: Local Development
items.detail: One workstation; UI, API and schema per app; EAL, UME and services alongside. Available now.

items.label: Central Development
items.detail: Independent deployables, published SDK, non-loopback origins, release manifests. Planned.

items.label: QA / UAT
items.detail: Production-shaped environments promoted by manifest with evidence gates. Planned.

items.label: Production
items.detail: Customer-controlled install: identity federation, secret references, backup and restore drills, SLOs. Planned.

blocks.caption: Promotion is by immutable release manifest and gate evidence, never by rebuilding.

rows: Build, verify and use applications on the platform host; every feature in this guide
Shared development landscape for a team
Independent qualification of a release manifest

blocks.text: Testing exists at every stage already: typecheck, contract tests and browser qualification run inside Local Development for each build, and Eval Studio evaluates the platform and applications continuously. What is missing is separate infrastructure for later environments, not testing.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL about environments
plPrompts.prompt: What development, testing, staging, and production environments does the platform support today, and which are planned? Be explicit about what is available in this workspace. Do not build anything.

title: Configuration, infrastructure, deployment and runtime management
prompt: How does the platform handle application configuration, infrastructure, deployment, and runtime management?
summary: Configuration is derived from the confirmed landscape and injected through an allow-list; infrastructure is a schema, two processes and reserved ports; deployment is a recorded lifecycle with rollback; runtime management is a managed runtime inside PL plus the Control Center for the platform's own services.

rows.label: Configuration
rows.value: The app receives only the keys its profile allows (its database URL, its ports, EAL origins). Keys outside the allow-list are refused, which is how platform credentials stay out of generated apps.

rows.label: Infrastructure
rows.value: Provisioned by the deployer: CREATE ROLE with NOBYPASSRLS and a random password, schema, migrations from the release, ports verified and reserved in-process.

rows.label: Deployment
rows.value: A lifecycle with durable records: staging directory, atomic rename, per-file hashes, activation only after Business Review, rollback to the previous release directory.

rows.label: Runtime management
rows.value: The managed runtime adopts running processes after a PL restart and restarts lost ones; the Control Center starts, stops and monitors PL, EAL, UME, EKG and the other services with an approval policy.

blocks.text: Secrets are file-based on the workstation today. Secret references through a key vault, containers and a service manager are part of the deployment foundation for customer sites.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL how deployment is managed
plPrompts.prompt: How does the platform handle application configuration, infrastructure, deployment, and runtime management for a generated application? Do not build anything.
